meister40-set.summary: On publishing the Council of Trent: strong resistance everywhere over Gallican liberties. In Paris Morosini lobbied the Sorbonne and the royal council, and told Henri III that a Most Christian king should accept the council without conditions. The King answered that the clergy, above all the Archbishop of Lyon, were the ones opposing it.
meister40-set.en:
[f. 32r] […] concerning the publication of the Council of Trent, [I] have not failed and do not fail to do all the most
effective offices, and [to oppose (?)], so that it be done without any limitation or condition; but in fact I find very
great resistance in everyone, for they will not in any way hear anything said against this pretended liberty of the
Gallican church. And they say that in Spain too, in the kingdom of Aragon, they chose to accept it so as not to
prejudice their privileges;

R17.summary: A Morosini-period letter of 1587 in the Meister no. 40 key, filed by DECODE with the Bergamo/Nazareth despatches: it concerns the Duke of Lorraine and Guise, the German reiters, the Queen Mother and Schomberg.
R17.en:
[f. 233r] […] to try to remove the difficulties and mistrust and to bring in union, which alone can help the present
needs […].

[…] the Maréchal de Retz, who greatly fears these events, concludes, in a long conversation he had with me today, that
unless Our Lord, as father of Christendom, interposes his authority vigorously both with the King and with the others,
he sees no remedy to keep this kingdom from being lost. [So] I, to understand what he meant that His Holiness could do
in this case — after a long circuit of words he said that this meant seeking to understand the claims of
the one party and the other, giving right and wrong to whoever had it, and then working, with his supreme authority, to
make everyone content with what is fair; and that there was no other remedy for this evil.

[f.

system: Meister no. 40 (1587): homophonic letters, clusters and common words in 1-3 digit figures run together without separators, three-digit dotted nomenclator, nulls 8x.
